title: Value-Chain Mapping
equation: Component Position = Visibility to User × Evolution Stage
hook: Stop custom-building things you could buy off the shelf for a fraction of the cost.
statement: Map each part of your business by how visible and how mature it is. Then you know where to focus.
explainer: You can't plan strategy on ground you can't see. Mapping each piece shows what's new and worth building, and what's become a commodity you should just buy.
sop: List every component your product depends on, top to bottom.
Rate each one's Visibility to User from 1 to 10.
Rate its Evolution Stage from 1 to 10, brand new to commodity.
Multiply and plot them on a simple map.
Build what's novel. Buy or outsource what's a commodity.
equation_example: A payment feature: Visibility to User 9 × Evolution Stage 8 = 72. Very visible and nearly a commodity, so buy it, don't build it. A low score flags something new and behind the scenes that might be worth building yourself.
question: Name one thing you're building custom that you could just buy.
closing_statement: Draw the map so you stop wandering.
caption:
Principle Nº 362: Value-Chain Mapping

Map each part of your business by how visible and how mature it is. Then you know where to focus.
